quality_assessment: Chapter covers the basics well but misses important features like hyperlink aliases and additional variables. Some examples reference non-existent editor schemes.

issues.description: Chapter only documents {path}, {line}, {column} variables but misses {host} and {wslprefix}
issues.current_content:
Available variables for hyperlink templates:

- `{path}`: Absolute or relative file path
- `{line}`: Line number of the match
- `{column}`: Column number of the match
issues.should_add: Document {host} variable for hostname in hyperlinks and {wslprefix} variable for WSL distro prefix (e.g., wsl$/Ubuntu)
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add two more variables to the Format Variables section:
- `{host}`: Machine hostname (set via environment)
- `{wslprefix}`: WSL distro prefix like wsl$/Ubuntu (Windows only)

issues.description: Chapter doesn't document built-in hyperlink aliases feature
issues.should_add: Document that ripgrep supports named aliases like 'vscode', 'default', 'none', 'file', 'kitty', 'macvim', 'textmate', 'vscode-insiders', 'vscodium', 'cursor', 'grep+'
issues.fix_suggestion: Add a new section 'Built-in Aliases' before 'Hyperlink Formats' section explaining that instead of full format strings, users can use short aliases. List all available aliases with their expanded formats.

issues.description: Chapter shows IntelliJ, Sublime, and Atom URL schemes but these are not built-in aliases
issues.current_content:
# IntelliJ/PyCharm/WebStorm
rg --hyperlink-format 'idea://open?file={path}&line={line}' pattern

# Sublime Text
rg --hyperlink-format 'subl://open?url=file://{path}&line={line}' pattern

# Atom
rg --hyperlink-format 'atom://open/?path={path}&line={line}' pattern
issues.should_be: Either remove these examples or clearly mark them as user-contributed/community formats (not built-in aliases). Focus on documented built-in aliases.
issues.fix_suggestion: Replace IntelliJ, Sublime, Atom examples with actual built-in aliases like 'cursor', 'macvim', 'textmate', 'kitty', 'grep+'. Move unsupported editor schemes to a separate 'Community Formats' or 'Custom Editor Integration' section.
issues.source_reference: crates/printer/src/hyperlink/aliases.rs (no aliases exist for IntelliJ, Sublime, or Atom)

issues.description: Chapter mentions 'default' format but doesn't explain it's platform-aware
issues.current_content:
# Default format (file path only)
rg --hyperlink-format default pattern
issues.fix_suggestion: Add explanation: 'The default alias uses RFC 8089 file:// scheme and is platform-aware. On Unix-like systems it includes the hostname ({host}), while on Windows it omits it for compatibility.'

issues.description: Chapter doesn't mention 'none' alias for explicitly disabling hyperlinks
issues.should_add: Document the 'none' alias which can be used to explicitly disable hyperlinks (useful for overriding config files)
issues.fix_suggestion: Add to Built-in Aliases section: 'none' - Explicitly disable hyperlinks (useful to override config file settings)

issues.description: Chapter doesn't show examples using built-in aliases
issues.should_add: Add examples showing usage of built-in aliases like 'vscode', 'kitty', 'file', etc.
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add Example 1b: Using built-in alias for VS Code:
```bash
rg --hyperlink-format vscode TODO
```
This is equivalent to the full format but more concise.

issues.description: Chapter doesn't explain how to set {host} and {wslprefix} environment variables
issues.should_add: Explain that {host} and {wslprefix} are set via HyperlinkEnvironment (typically by ripgrep automatically, or via grep-cli crate's hostname function)
issues.fix_suggestion: Add note: 'The {host} variable is automatically populated by ripgrep from your system hostname. The {wslprefix} variable is set on Windows when running in WSL.'

issues.description: Chapter doesn't document variable escaping syntax ({{ and }})
issues.should_add: Document how to include literal { and } characters in hyperlink formats using {{ and }}
issues.fix_suggestion: Add subsection 'Escaping Special Characters': To include literal braces in your hyperlink format, use double braces: `{{` for `{` and `}}` for `}`

positive_aspects: Clear introduction explaining what hyperlinks are and when they're useful
Good terminal compatibility list covering major terminal emulators
Helpful troubleshooting section with practical solutions
Good examples of file:// scheme usage
Covers conditional hyperlink usage in scripts
improvement_suggestions: Add comprehensive 'Built-in Aliases' section documenting all supported aliases
Update editor integration examples to focus on built-in aliases rather than unverified custom schemes
Add example showing the difference between 'default' and 'file' aliases
Document {host} and {wslprefix} variables with usage examples
Add section on variable escaping ({{ and }})
Consider adding a quick reference table mapping alias names to their expanded formats
Add example showing how 'none' alias can override config file settings
Clarify which examples are built-in vs. community/custom formats
